screenDefinitions.no_letters: not any Unicode isalpha in gloss
screenDefinitions.markup_or_escaped_entity: contains < or > or & " ' < > or decimal numeric entity
screenDefinitions.replacement_or_mojibake: U+FFFD or regex patterns for selected ?/?/? + U+0080-U+00BF sequences
screenDefinitions.control_character: any Unicode category beginning C, including format Cf
screenDefinitions.placeholder_pattern: case-insensitive FIXME|undefined|null|NaN|placeholder|untranslated as words; asterisk; repeated question mark; uppercase TODO. Spanish todo/Todo not included.
screenDefinitions.non_latin_script: any Hebrew U+0590-U+05FF, Greek U+0370-U+03FF or Cyrillic U+0400-U+04FF character

reviewerKind: AI assistant; no human translator review
status: Original automated audit plus bounded AI-assisted spot check and99 explicit local corrections; not human linguistic validation

candidateProvenance.matchingRule: An entire canonical KJV-reference verse must contain the same ordered original-word surfaces after Unicode NFC. No diacritics/punctuation stripped; no Strong-only or numerical-only alignment. Correspondence from the existing hash-bound KJV mapping supplies TAHOT occurrence IDs.
structuralRules: Ignore whitespace and Unicode Cf formatting controls only.

A standalone pe/samekh word with lemma strong:H???? and no morphology is appended to the preceding word for comparison only. The same exact paragraph letter must exist in that TAHOT token surface AND be classified as a punctuation segment, or the verse fails. The paragraph word contributes no translated meaning.
modifications: Extracted word gloss attributes from the pinned SWORD zText OSIS records.
Bound only entire verses with exactly matching ordered Hebrew/Aramaic source surfaces after the documented normalization.
Attached matching glosses to existing TAHOT occurrence IDs; did not modify original-language text or translate any glosses.
Excluded upstream empty/star placeholders and entries containing no letters.
Split the result into per-native-chapter JSON sidecars and supplied content SHA-256 hashes.
limitations: Spanish wording is a separate machine-assisted study layer, not the wording of the selected RVA translation.
Source glossary transliterates some names, e.g. Elohim, and may contain linguistic errors.
Many-to-many tokenization, differing diacritics, ketiv/qere differences, and unmatched passages receive no imported Spanish gloss.
Glosses are whole-token meanings, not per-morpheme segment translations or Spanish dictionary definitions.
No upstream linguistic quality assessment or native Hebrew-to-Spanish scholarly review was performed.
